items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: And, uh, in the rhythm section was Faith Marvel, piano, and that fellow named, drummer named Gene Hill, Al Morgan on bass, and me on banjo.

ctx.x: And, uh, Evan Hall on clarinet. Mm-hmm. Al Morgan on bass. Mm-hmm. And I believe he had Joe Strada on drums, yeah. And had a very fine banjo player in those days named Caffrey.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: that band was composed of Lee Collin on trumpet Evan Hall on clarinet Albert Morgan on bass and Caffrey... now Joe Wynn he brought us up there and he stole Albert Morgan and Edmund Hall out of that band and put them with the band we had

ctx.x: that's the one I was telling you about Caffrey that was with the band remember I mentioned their name? yeah that was with the band that when we first got there they was with another guy working for the guy up there Prince Morris but Joe Wynn had came in and picked up a group and brought us there and when we got there he took out of that band that band was composed of Lee Collin on trumpet Evan Hall on clarinet Albert Morgan on bass and Caffrey I always remember Caffrey Caffrey Dairnsbury and they had Oil on…

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: I had a group up there... he was with some band... we had him over to Johnny and Lindsey's house... old Al Morgan.

ctx.x: One more question on the record. Who did the singing?

Oh yeah, the singing came about, and that came about, Alvin Morgan always could, you like to sing and scat like, looks like everybody was trying to do that, see. And Alvin could do that, so he was the one decided to say, yeah, well let me scat this, and say, let me take one on scat, you see. And I think that was supposed to be a band or solo for them, so as he did it so good, they just let it go through at that, you see. That was Alvin Morgan during the scatting, yeah. Al Morgan? Yeah, Al Morgan, yeah. His name…
Took men out of Sydney's band? Who's Sydney? Sydney Desby.
